chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn A'dhina, from Abban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Ja'far at-Tayyar saying:

We were with Mu'awiya, along with me, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Umar ibn Umm Salama, and Usama ibn Zayd. A conversation occurred between me and Mu'awiya, so I said to Mu'awiya: I heard the Messenger of God saying: 'I am worthier of the believers than themselves, then my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib is worthier of the believers than themselves. When Ali is martyred, then al-Hasan ibn Ali is worthier of the believers than themselves, then his son al-Husayn after him is worthier of the believers than themselves. When he is martyred, then his son Ali ibn al-Husayn is worthier of the believers than themselves, and you will reach him, O Ali. Then his son Muhammad ibn Ali is worthier of the believers than themselves, and you will reach him, O Husayn. Then they will be completed by twelve Imams, nine of whom are from the progeny of al-Husayn.'
Abdullah ibn Ja'far said: So I called upon al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Umar ibn Umm Salama, and Usama ibn Zayd to witness, and they witnessed.
Sulaym said: And I heard that from Salman al-Farisi, al-Miqdad, and Abu Dharr, and they mentioned that they heard it from the Messenger of God.
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve Imams mentioned in the hadith of Sulaym ibn Qays and what is their order of succession?
ai.summary: This narration from Sulaym ibn Qays highlights the concept of *Al-Wilayah al-Takwiniyyah* (divine authority) by linking Ali’s precedence to the Prophet’s own, establishing a clear line of succession through the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as a foundational text for the doctrine of the Twelve Imams, explicitly noting that nine of them will descend from Husayn, a detail that underscores the continuity of leadership despite the political shifts of the early Caliphate. The inclusion of multiple companions (Salman, Abu Dharr, Miqdad) as witnesses reinforces the authenticity and widespread acceptance of this specific chain of authority in Shia tradition.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (27) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from Ali bin Ibraheem bin Hashim from his father from ibn Abu Omayr from Abban bin Ayyash that Sulaym bin Qayss al-Hilali had said: I have heard Abdullah bin Ja’far at-Tayyar saying:

One day Al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Abdullah bin Abbas, Umar bin Umm Salama, Ussama bin Zayd and I were with Mo’awiya. I said to him: “I have heard the Prophet (S) saying: “I am worthier of the believers than themselves then my brother Ali bin Abu Talib will be worthier of the believers than themselves. If he is martyred then his son al-Hasan will be worthier of the believers than themselves then after him al-Husayn will be worthier of the believers than themselves. If he is martyred, his son Ali bin al-Husayn will be worthier of the believers than themselves then his son Muhammad bin Ali will be worthier of the believers than themselves then the rest of the twelve imams, nine of whom are from the progeny of al-Husayn.”
I asked al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Abdullah bin Abbas, Umar bin Umm Salama and Ussama bin Zayd to witness of that (the Prophet (S) had said so) and they witnessed.”
Sulaym said: “I have heard that from Salman al-Farisi, al-Miqdad and Abu Tharr that they have heard it from the Prophet (S).”
